title: U.S. House · Oregon's 2nd District
area: Eastern, southern and much of rural Oregon, covering roughly 20 counties including Medford, Klamath Falls, Bend's eastern edges, and Ontario.

context.text: Incumbent Cliff Bentz defeated Peter Larson and Andrea Carr with 79.6% in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Chris Beck led a six-way Democratic primary field with 34.4% of the vote, ahead of Mary Doyle, Rebecca Mueller, Dawn Rasmussen, Patty Snow and Peter Quince; Ballotpedia noted this was the most-contested Oregon U.S. House primary field in 2026.

summary.text: Cliff Bentz is the Republican nominee for re-election to Oregon's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 2021. He is a third-generation Oregonian and former state legislator from Ontario.

background.text: Raised on his family's cattle ranches in Harney County; graduated cum laude from Eastern Oregon State College and earned a J.D. from Lewis and Clark Law School.

Practiced water and ranch-reorganization law in Ontario, Oregon, becoming a partner at the Yturri, O'Kief, Rose and Burnham firm; chaired the Oregon Water Resources Commission and the Ontario 8C public school board.
Served in the Oregon House of Representatives (2008-2018) and Oregon State Senate (2018-2020) before being elected to Congress in 2020.

positions.summary: Voted for a motion to refer H. Res. 863 (impeachment of DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas) to committee, stating that Mayorkas' implementation of Biden administration border policy 'resulted in the worst mass illegal migration into the United States that we have ever experienced.'
positions.quote: There is no question that Secretary Mayorkas has failed to carry out his duties as cabinet secretary, putting the American people at serious and decades-long risk. His implementation of the Biden border policies has resulted in the worst mass illegal migration into the United States that we have ever experienced.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Subcommittees on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Health; Energy) and the Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittees on Federal Lands; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries).

In the 118th Congress (2023-2024), chaired the House Natural Resources Committee's Subcommittee on Water, Oceans, and Wildlife and served on the House Judiciary Committee (Subcommittees on Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust; Courts, Intellectual Property, and the Internet).

As an Oregon state senator (2019-2020), served as Vice-Chair of the Senate Finance and Revenue Committee and Co-Vice Chair of the Tax Expenditures Committee, and sat on the Joint Transportation Committee, the Environment and Natural Resources Committee, and the Judiciary and Ballot Measure 110 Implementation Committee.

summary.text: Chris Beck is the Democratic nominee for Oregon's 2nd Congressional District. He is a former Oregon state representative who later worked as a rural economic policy advisor at the USDA.

background.text: Attended Oregon public schools; earned a bachelor's degree from Brown University (1985) and a graduate degree from Harvard University's Kennedy School of Government (2005).

Began a career in public service as legislative staff for the Oregon Legislature, then was elected as an Oregon State Representative and served six years; later spent six years as a rural economic policy advisor at USDA headquarters in Washington, D.C.
Worked as a land-conservation real estate negotiator for the Trust for Public Land, helping conserve land in the Columbia Gorge and elsewhere in Oregon.

priorities.text: Health care access: describes quality health care as a human right and cites rural hospital and clinic closures making basic and emergency care harder to reach in the district.

Housing: says the free market alone has never produced affordable housing and calls for public assistance and incentives, with low-cost housing built into existing Main Street neighborhoods rather than on farm and forest land.

Trade and immigration: opposes the tariffs imposed during the Trump administration, which he says have hurt rural export markets, and calls for repealing them alongside a 'sensible, bipartisan approach to legal immigration.'

positions.summary: Says the current administration, 'with the blind support of our Congressman,' has cut Medicaid with no plan for comprehensive health care reform, and calls quality health care a human right.
positions.quote: Quality Health Care is a Human Right.

positions.summary: Says housing must be built, with public assistance and incentives, concentrated in existing Main Street neighborhoods rather than scattered onto farm and forest resource land.
Calls the tariffs imposed under the Trump administration 'careless and haphazard' and says he would work to repeal them.
